SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaints: Feeling generally unwell for ~5 days, cough (mostly dry with occasional sputum), runny nose, sore throat, episodic shortness of breath (no chest pain), subjective fevers with night sweats, transient diarrhea on day 1 (resolved), generalized muscle/joint stiffness.
- Onset & course: Began Saturday (≈5 days ago) after evening out; symptoms persist.
- Associated symptoms denied/absent: Chest pain, significant ear pain, persistent GI symptoms.
- Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus; hypertension; overweight/obesity acknowledged.
- Medications:
  • Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented  
  • Aspirin intermittently – dose/route/frequency not documented
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Social history: Lives with wife; factory worker (steel parts). Alcohol ~9 pints beer/week. Occasional smoking; currently using vaporizer to cut down. No children at home.

Objective:
- Tele-consultation (no in-person examination or vitals).
- Doctor audible findings: nasal congestion/sniffles; patient speaking in full sentences but reports dyspnea.
- No other physical examination performed.
- Investigations: None to date.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Upper respiratory tract infection / probable viral illness
   - Assessment: Likely viral URTI or early influenza; mild/moderate symptoms with subjective fever and cough; no objective evidence of bacterial chest infection at present.
   - Differential diagnosis: Early bacterial lower respiratory tract infection; COVID-19 (not discussed); allergic rhinitis with superimposed viral illness.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; patient advised to monitor temperature and symptoms.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Symptomatic care: Rest, maintain hydration, regular Paracetamol as needed for fever/discomfort.  
     • Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet TID x 5 days; start only if no improvement or worsening within 24–48 h.  
     • Safety-net advice: Return for review or seek urgent care if increasing shortness of breath, chest pain, persistent high fever, or no improvement by next week.

2. Shortness of breath
   - Assessment: Likely secondary to viral illness; no red-flag features elicited.
   - Investigations planned: None immediately; monitor; consider in-person exam and pulse oximetry if symptoms worsen.
   - Treatment planned: As above; delayed antibiotics if progression; reinforce smoking cessation to aid respiratory health.

3. Chronic conditions (Type 2 diabetes, hypertension, overweight)
   - Assessment: Stable on current therapy per patient report; no acute issues raised.
   - Treatment planned: Continue Metformin and Lisinopril; encourage lifestyle measures (weight control, alcohol moderation, smoking cessation). Routine chronic disease follow-up not covered in this call.

Quality checks:

• Missing/expected elements: No vital signs, pulse oximetry, or throat/chest examination possible via phone; vaccination history (influenza/COVID) not obtained; medication doses not documented; allergies confirmed only verbally.  
• Internal conflicts: Patient initially said breathing “fine” then “not good/short of breath” – conflict noted. Cough described as “mostly dry” yet also admits “wee bit” sputum – minor inconsistency.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; some conversational digressions and mild background noise but clinically usable.
